Action Plan:
1) Urgent hospital evaluation for suspected postpartum pulmonary embolism (PE). Patient will self-transport to the hospital with the baby (ambulance available if needed). Bring baby and essential items; do not delay. The clinician emphasized PE risk in the postpartum/post-C-section context and outlined ED evaluation to rule out PE; if a clot is confirmed, anticoagulation or clot-directed therapy may be started.
2) Immediate medication management: Do not take any further codeine-containing analgesics until evaluated in the ED.
3) Home pulse assessment: Patient was instructed to palpate her pulse at the wrist and count heartbeats for assessment; patient performed the count (30) and reported the heart rate as “slightly fast” on exam.
4) If a clot is confirmed in ED: anticoagulation or clot-directed therapy as indicated.
5) Follow-up: Return to the ED or seek urgent care if symptoms worsen or fail to improve.
6) Verbal consent: Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Note on consent: Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden shortness of breath (dyspnea) ongoing for about 1 hour; dyspnea occurs at rest while watching TV.
- History of present illness: Started within the last hour; also reports a new cough beginning yesterday; no chest pain at rest; chest soreness with very deep breaths.
- Postpartum status: 4 weeks after cesarean delivery; currently with baby at home.
- Past medical history: Recently underwent C-section; no other medical problems reported.
- Medications: Regular use of codeine for pain after C-section; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen (allergic reaction not specified).
- Social history: Baby at home; partner at work.
- Review of symptoms: No fever reported; no unilateral leg symptoms discussed.
- Special notes: C-section scar tender; chest wall tenderness noted; patient reports heart racing.
- Vitals/measurements provided by patient: No formal vitals given; patient reports tachycardia; clinician noted heart rate as “slightly fast” on bedside assessment.
- Additional info: No oxygen saturation or imaging results available at this time.

Objective:
- Cardiac/vascular: Patient describes heart rate as “slightly fast” during assessment.
- Respiratory: Shortness of breath at rest; new cough starting yesterday; chest soreness on deep inspiration.
- Chest wall: Chest wall tenderness including C-section scar.
- Abdomen/pelvis: Postpartum status (4 weeks since C-section); no stated abdominal findings.

- Other: No documented fever, no other acute illnesses noted; no oxygen saturation or formal vitals recorded beyond subjective report and clinician’s note of tachycardia.

Assessment & Plan:
1) Working concern: Pulmonary embolism (PE) in the postpartum patient after recent cesarean section
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Pulmonary embolism (PE). Likelihood: High (DDx step3_ranked_ddx indicates PE as high likelihood in this postpartum/post-C-section patient with acute dyspnea and tachycardia).
   - Differential diagnosis (from DDx consistent with this presentation): Pneumonia (Medium); Acute bronchitis (Medium).
   - Investigations planned: Hospital ED evaluation to rule out PE; specific tests (e.g., imaging or labs) to be determined by ED clinicians.
   - Treatment planned: If a clot is confirmed, anticoagulation or clot-directed therapy will be provided as indicated.
   - Referrals: Emergency department evaluation; possible inpatient management if PE is confirmed.
   - Rationale: Postpartum period (4 weeks post-C-section) is a hypercoagulable state; sudden SOB with tachycardia raises concern for PE. The clinician advised ED evaluation to exclude PE and to manage promptly if present.

2) Possible infectious or inflammatory pulmonary process
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Pneumonia or acute bronchitis (in the differential; pneumonia as a possibility given new cough and dyspnea).
   - Differential diagnosis (from DDx consistent with this presentation): Pneumonia (Medium); Acute bronchitis (Medium); others less likely (e.g., asthma, bronchospasm, other thoracic etiologies) per the DDx.
   - Investigations planned: Not explicitly specified; ED evaluation will determine appropriate tests (imaging, labs) if indicated.
   - Treatment planned: Not specified at this time; management contingent on ED findings.
   - Referrals: If infectious etiology is suspected, follow-up with primary care as appropriate after ED assessment.
   - Rationale: New cough with dyspnea could reflect infection, though absence of fever and lack of imaging/culture data in the transcript means ED assessment is prioritized.
